=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1313-1317 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new check fires whenever an invocation is a push and has a warning. The same fixed string is appended for every matching invocation. This is a correct, scoped tightening of the trust boundary — it ensures the guard asks for confirmation when a `GIT_DIR+=` / `GIT_WORK_TREE+=` override cannot be resolved and the session checkout's branch is not itself merged. Without this addition, the original PR left a hole where `GIT_DIR+=<path> git push origin HEAD` from a session checkout on `main` would not block (no merged PR for `main`) and would not prompt — bash appends the override to the inherited variable, so git could push from a different repository than the checkout.
  WHY: A push whose effective repository cannot be resolved locally would be allowed because the existing targets loop only blocks when an *explicit* destination matches a merged PR, and falls through silently when the session checkout's current branch has no merged PR. The new check promotes the unresolved-repository case to a confirmation request, restoring fail-safe behaviour for the appended-override path.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:832-840 and tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:842-855 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The two new tests cover exactly the missing case from the original PR's `test_appended_git_override_falls_back_without_using_rhs` — the session checkout is on `main` (no merged PR) and the appended override points to a worktree whose branch does have a merged PR. The tests assert both the new "could not resolve git push repository" warning substring and the `"permissionDecision": "ask"` outcome. Both cases (`GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`) are parametrised.
  WHY: Without the LAST RUN DIFF code change these tests would fail (no warning substring, no `ask` decision). They pin the runtime behaviour to the new check and to the byte-identical template copy.
- changelog.d/6286-pr-merge-guard-appended-git-dir.md:1-6 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment was reworded in the LAST RUN DIFF to reflect the new "asks for confirmation when the checkout check does not block" behaviour, replacing the prior wording that implied the guard already covered both branches of the appended-override path. The replacement is accurate.
  WHY: Not a runtime defect — the wording matches the LAST RUN DIFF's actual behaviour. Flagged for completeness against the previous text.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:251-255 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_is_unquoted_fd_prefix(command, digits, operator)` is defined in both guard copies but has zero call sites anywhere in the repository (no production caller, no test caller). The IO_NUMBER detection the function would perform is implemented inline inside `_shell_segments_with_operators` using `last_word_span` tracking. Two pass-1 reviewers flagged this independently.
  WHY: It does not fail at runtime — the function is never invoked. The defect is maintainability: a future reader may assume it is wired into the redirect-parsing path and modify it expecting behavioural effect, and any future linter will flag it as unused. Both guard copies must stay byte-identical, so removal from one copy requires removal from the other.
